title: Turn-cohort allocator: proactive KV prefetch, priority eviction, and slab packing for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: reduce P95 token latency and GPU memory fragmentation for mixed prompt/response workloads by introducing a turn-cohort allocator that coalesces short-turn traffic into micro-cohorts, performs proactive KV prefetch based on prefix similarity, and uses slab packing to reduce tensor waste. This ticket designs the allocator heuristics, an offline simulation harness, a canary experiment in staging, and an incremental rollout plan.
motivation: Mixed-length dialogue workloads (short user prompts followed by long system responses and vice versa) create fragmentation in both batching slots and KV residency. Existing continuous batcher policies either hold slots too long (increasing latency) or evict too aggressively (increasing KV recompute and GPU work). We propose a complementary approach: group requests into 'turn-cohorts' based on recent turn lengths and prefix similarity, proactively warm KV entries for high-similarity cohorts, and pack tensors into GPU slabs using an adaptive trailing-compression heuristic to reduce wasted memory from padding.
approach: Allocator: assign incoming requests to a short-lived turn-cohort bucket (30-120ms target lifetime) keyed by: recent per-session average turn length, high-level prompt tag, and fast L2 prefix-similarity hash.
KV prefetch: for cohorts with >50% prefix-similarity, trigger background KV warmup for the most likely next-turn keys using a capped prefetch budget per GPU (configurable slot).

Eviction scoring: compute per-slot eviction score = alpha * age + beta * last-prefetch-score + gamma * compute-cost-estimate. Tune weights to prioritize evicting slots with low reuse probability but high memory pressure impact.

Slab packing: at allocation time, group tensors from short prompts into contiguous slabs and apply trailing-compression that merges small tail paddings from adjacent tensors into a shared buffer to reduce padding overhead.
Fallbacks: when prefetch budget is exceeded or for low-confidence cohorts, fall back to existing length-priority batcher. Disable prefetch in low-memory mode.
Instrumentation: add cohort_id and prefetch_tag to tracing headers for downstream tracing and attribution.
acceptance_criteria: Staging experiment shows >=8% reduction in P95 token-latency for mixed-length synthetic workload compared to baseline with equivalent throughput
GPU memory fragmentation metric (measured by slab_free_ratio) improves by >=12% at 90th percentile during peak load
KV hit ratio for turned-cohorts increases by >10% without increasing overall GPU compute by more than 3%
No customer-facing error increase in staging; error rate stays within baseline noise (<=0.5% relative change)
Canary rollout plan validated, and feature flag toggles available to disable prefetch or slab packing independently
experiment_plan: Offline simulation: run 2 weeks of historical traffic through the simulator with three cohort policies (aggressive-prefetch, conservative-prefetch, no-prefetch) and slab packing on/off
Staging canary: deploy allocator behind feature-flag to 10% of routing nodes; run 48h A/B against baseline traffic using traffic mirror of production mixed-length endpoints
Post-canary analysis: compare the metrics above; inspect trace samples for KV warmup mispredictions and slab packing edge cases (alignment failures, OOMs)
Gradual rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 3 days each, with automatic rollback threshold on P95 latency or error delta exceeding configured limits
Post-release telemetry: add cohort-specific dashboards and alerting for kv.hit_rate_by_cohort and slab_free_ratio regression
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect prefetches increase GPU compute and degrade latency. Mitigation: cap prefetch budget per GPU and set conservative confidence threshold; expose kill-switch.

Risk: slab packing introduces alignment bugs or increases kernel launch overhead. Mitigation: run microbenchmarks for common tensor sizes and add runtime validation in staging (compare outputs with baseline), enable slab packing only for size classes with validated improvements.

Risk: eviction scoring complexity increases CPU overhead. Mitigation: implement scoring as lightweight fixed-point arithmetic and profile CPU impact; fall back to simpler age-only eviction if overhead >2% CPU.
Risk: subtle regressions for enterprise customers with pinned model versions. Mitigation: add per-customer opt-out and test with dedicated capacity nodes before global rollout.
